grh_583f0c32a5e970c8f91b.title: My True Valentine
paragraphs: In 1925, seamstress Emily Cobb is engaged to Don Burns, a young man with a wild reputation who is trying to straighten out his life. After a machine-works robbery, watchman Joel Sims identifies one of the nearly identical Burns brothers before being shot to death. Don's brother Sandy is known to be away, leaving Don without an alibi, and Don is convicted despite insisting he is innocent. He refuses to let Emily tie her life to his and spends years in prison while she eventually builds a successful fashion business in Chicago. Fifteen years later Emily returns to Rivers End on Valentine's Day, torn over whether to marry a kind, successful man who loves her even though she still loves Don. At the same time Don returns after being cleared when the real killer confesses while already serving a life sentence on another charge. Emily decides before knowing Don is back that she cannot marry anyone else, and Dr. Christian reunites the two, suggesting that after all those lost years Valentine's Day is an appropriate day for their wedding.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on February 14, 1940. It is listed as episode 67 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_58fc0a6d8176e75b9152.title: Jenny
paragraphs: Britt carries a wounded stranger to the isolated cabin of Jenny Garver, a lonely woman who has spent years being mocked for her appearance and awkwardness. The man proves to be a wanted killer, but Jenny refuses to give him up because, for the first time, someone seems to need her; when the sheriff's posse surrounds the cabin, she even fires to protect him. The fugitive finally dies from his wounds, ending the standoff. Afterward the town notices that Jenny carries herself with a new confidence, as though the brief experience of being needed has changed the way she sees herself.

paragraphs: This original musical drama follows exiled Polish composer Frédéric Chopin as his longing for his occupied homeland becomes inseparable from his music and his turbulent relationship with writer George Sand. paragraphs: Government clerk Cadogan West is found dead on an Underground train roof with some, but not all, of Britain's secret submarine plans in his pocket. Holmes traces the missing papers to spy Hugo Oberstein's house beside the railway and lures Colonel Valentine Walter there with a coded advertisement.
